title: Finding the Fenn Treasure
summary: Josh and Chuck cover the Forrest Fenn treasure hunt: the bronze treasure chest Fenn hid in the Rocky Mountains, his poem-based clues in his memoir The Thrill of the Chase, the tens of thousands of searchers, the deaths and rescues, the legal and ethical controversies, and the 2020 discovery by an anonymous finder, including the role of Jack Stuef's close reading of the poem. The episode opens with book-sales and shout-out banter and closes with listener mail about Cisco, a correction to the Buffet episode.
topics: treasure chest in the Rocky Mountains

segments.title: Opening banter and book sales
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck joke around, shout out a listener, mention the Stuff You Should Know book nearing 100,000 copies sold, and set up the Fenn treasure topic.

segments.title: Overview of the Fenn treasure hunt
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the treasure hunt: a chest of gold, jewels, and artifacts hidden by Forrest Fenn, with a poem-based map. About 350,000 people searched, some quitting jobs to move to the Rockies.

segments.title: Forrest Fenn's early life and art career
segments.summary: Fenn grew up visiting Yellowstone, became an Air Force pilot who flew combat missions in Vietnam, became a pacifist, and moved to Santa Fe in 1992 to deal in art, especially Native American art and artifacts, running galleries and selling to celebrities.

segments.title: Looting controversy and FBI investigation
segments.summary: Fenn is criticized by Native American communities and archaeologists for undocumented excavations. An FBI undercover operation led to a 2009 raid, and no charges were reported. The hosts describe his trickster persona and his sale of master forgeries.

segments.title: The treasure chest and Fenn's cancer
segments.summary: Fenn's father took his own life after cancer. Fenn planned a similar end in the Rockies, leaving a treasure chest with him, but he beat cancer. He then published his memoir with a poem containing the clues.

segments.title: Reading the poem and early clues
segments.summary: The hosts read the poem aloud and discuss its nine clues, the elevation and location hints, and the first clue 'begin it where warm waters halt', plus over-interpretations such as reading 'below the home of Brown' as an outhouse.
topics: begin it where warm waters halt

segments.title: Searcher deaths, rescues, and Fenn's response
segments.summary: Several searchers died, including Jeff Murphy, Eric Ashby, Randy Bilyeu, a priest named Wallace, and Michael Sexton near Dinosaur National Monument. Fenn responded that people should learn to swim rather than drain the pool.

segments.title: Damage to public lands and the stalker
segments.summary: Some searchers dug in parks and cemeteries, causing damage and arrests. Francisco Chavez harassed the Fenn family and was placed on probation; another man threatened the house with an axe.

segments.title: The discovery and the anonymous finder
segments.summary: In June 2020 Fenn announced the chest had been found. An anonymous finder who wished to keep the location private was identified amid conspiracy claims; a misleading blaze had led searchers astray, and a lawsuit by Barbara Anderson led to the identification of Jack Stuef.

segments.title: Jack Stuef's solve and Fenn's legacy
segments.summary: Jack Stuef, a former Onion writer and medical student, cracked the clues by close reading the poem and Fenn's interviews, and visited the spot many times. Fenn died in September 2020 at age 90. The hosts mention a documentary and a planned movie.

segments.title: Listener mail about Cisco
segments.summary: A listener who works for Cisco corrects the Buffet episode, saying most Cisco food is fresh rather than frozen. The hosts also mention a plug for his gaming channel.
